# Fixture: recovery_expr

A non-fatal error in one header that silently drops a call in another
(B-27 review). Two translation units:

- `main.c` includes `h1.h` and `h2.h`. `h1.h` declares `g` with a
  parameter of the unknown type `undefined_t`: an error (not fatal) on
  `h1.h` line 8. `h2.h` defines `static int k(void)`, which calls `g`.
  Clang suppresses follow-on errors at uses of the invalid `g`, so the
  call in `h2.h` becomes an expression with errors (`RecoveryExpr`, checked
  with Clang 20's `-ast-dump`), is not recorded, and no diagnostic names
  `h2.h`.
- `other.c` defines `g` and `other`, and parses cleanly.

Expected facts: `k` is a definition in `h2.h` with no call edges; the only
diagnostic is an error in `h1.h`, in unit `main.c`. A verifier that trusted
`h2.h` would contradict "`k` calls `g`" and confirm "`k` does not call
`g`". The compilation database is generated by the test.
